image_inspection.observed: The diagram moves from initial work through decision and creation to group work, stopped work, a blog post, and archive. The reopen branch requires a shepherd plus liaison and team consensus; missing either prerequisite ends in not continuing. The return arrow reaches Decision.
image_inspection.interpretation: The shared leadership and consensus prerequisites are retained. No additional mandatory approval beyond those prerequisites is inferred from the diagram/prose loop difference.

tokenization_and_hashing.normalization: Lowercase text before regex token extraction; queries themselves are lowercase.
tokenization_and_hashing.query_string_hash: SHA256 of the exact UTF-8 query string, excluding JSON framing.
tokenization_and_hashing.token_hash: SHA256 of extracted lowercase tokens joined by one ASCII space, encoded as UTF-8.
tokenization_and_hashing.query_file_hash: SHA256 of the complete JSONL file bytes, including the final newline.

R_fidelity_review.input: Calls to an existing assembly macro and the compiler references to its name.
R_fidelity_review.state: A behavior-preserving renamed macro coexists with a deprecated entry point during a transition.
R_fidelity_review.action: Rename the implementation and feature gate, retarget internal references, and forward deprecated calls.
R_fidelity_review.output: Identical macro behavior plus a deprecation warning directing callers to the renamed implementation and explaining the old name's future semantic change.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: Existing behavior remains available; the forwarding path preserves compatibility during the transition.

R_claim_support.claim: Behavior-preserving rename and renamed feature gate
Compiler retargeting, forwarding, and warning content

caveats: No choice is made between the unresolved feature gates for the deprecated macro.
The future replacement assembly interface is not implemented or assumed.
Future semantic change is described only because the initial warning contract explicitly requires it.

R_fidelity_review.input: A name lookup through a generic bound or trait object and its explicitly selected traits.
R_fidelity_review.state: An ancestor's same-name member is introduced only implicitly, or conflicting traits are explicitly present.
R_fidelity_review.action: Prefer the descendant member in the implicit-conflict case, retain other ancestor members, and apply the rule recursively.
R_fidelity_review.output: A selected descendant member, an ambiguity error for the retained explicit or peer conflicts, or explicitly qualified access to either distinct member.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: Already accepted programs remain accepted; qualified access persists; name lookup does not become overriding.

R_claim_support.claim: Generic/trait-object lookup and implicit conflict selection
Already accepted programs preserved and no overriding

caveats: No general multiple-inheritance solution is supplied.
Explicitly selected conflicts and unresolved peer conflicts remain errors.
Use-declaration behavior and possible future terminology decisions are not changed.

R_fidelity_review.input: An unsafe assembly template with input/output expressions, operand directions, register constraints, clobbers, and flags.
R_fidelity_review.state: Input registers initially hold their declared expression values; ordinary outputs may be written at any time.
R_fidelity_review.action: Keep ordinary outputs from sharing registers, allow declared late-output reuse under the read-before-write condition, then execute the assembly.
R_fidelity_review.output: Each retained output register is copied to its destination after execution; discarded outputs are excluded.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: All input values must be consumed before a reused register is written as a late output; declared constraints and behavior flags remain effective.
caveats: The late-write condition is a correctness obligation, not a claim that the compiler automatically verifies instruction timing.
No future memory operands, label operands, automatic call-clobber sets, or other deferred features are added.
Illustrative source code is not silently corrected or independently validated.

R_fidelity_review.input: A chartered project group whose active work has stopped, and a later possible request to reactivate it.
R_fidelity_review.state: Archival is a current, potentially reversible status and may occur for completion, lack of time, blockage, or abandonment.
R_fidelity_review.action: Announce archival, publish an account of outputs and process, archive infrastructure, and gate reactivation on assigned leadership and parent-team consensus.
R_fidelity_review.output: A public account excluding private feedback, a read-only repository, archived communication spaces, and active infrastructure only after reactivation prerequisites.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: Private feedback remains omitted; both leadership roles and consensus are required; earlier decisions are reassessed after significant elapsed time.

R_claim_support.claim: Stopping active work and nonpermanent archival

caveats: The query concerns project groups, avoiding the separate liaison ambiguity for working groups.
No universal formation-by-formal-proposal rule is imposed over the text's team-specific consensus procedures.
The diagram's return to Decision is not treated as an additional mandatory approval beyond the shared leadership and consensus prerequisites.
No strict universal definition of shepherd is invented.

R_fidelity_review.input: One load-balancer service definition with mixed port protocols, including the same number under two protocols.
R_fidelity_review.state: The proposed mixed-protocol support is active; a validation limitation previously rejected this case.
R_fidelity_review.action: Accept the mixed definition and pass it to the existing load-balancer controller.
R_fidelity_review.output: Application exposure determined by the controller and backing service's capabilities, with one address as a conditional goal.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: Acceptance does not guarantee uniform support across implementations; activation-control alternatives remain unresolved.

R_claim_support.claim: Acceptance of mixed protocols and same-number example

caveats: No final activation mechanism is chosen from the annotation and merging alternatives.
No universal provider outcome or unconditional single-address realization is asserted.
The source's test-plan and graduation placeholders are not treated as functional requirements.
The previously described implementation is not presented as evidence of a later outcome.

R_fidelity_review.input: Shared and per-instance configuration files, existing command-line flags, and an optional remote shared-configuration refresh.
R_fidelity_review.state: Instance-specific parameters use their own top-level Kind in the existing component API group; file objects are initially kept separate.
R_fidelity_review.action: Read the instance file through its canonical flag, reject cross-placement, and let existing flags override file values.
R_fidelity_review.output: Effective configuration combining shared settings and isolated instance settings; remote shared replacement does not replace instance settings.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: The Kind naming convention, initial file boundary, flag compatibility and precedence, and refresh isolation are preserved.

R_claim_support.claim: Existing API group and Kind naming convention
Canonical instance flag and initial file boundary

caveats: The remote-refresh statement describes the source's node-component configuration path and does not require every component to implement remote refresh.
The query retains the exact generic Kind naming convention without inventing a complete schema.
Cross-placement is prohibited initially, without ruling out the text's future possibility.
No immediate flag removal, fixed deprecation release, automatic value detection, or mandatory delivery implementation is added.
The conflicting draft-year metadata and unresolved command-line non-goal TODO are not settled.

R_fidelity_review.input: Profile metadata and dedicated fields when a workload object is created, followed by later update requests.
R_fidelity_review.state: Neither, one, or both representations may be present; older node agents may need backfilled metadata.
R_fidelity_review.action: Reconcile representations in the API server, validate equality when both are present, and remove the fields-to-metadata backfill in N+4.
R_fidelity_review.output: Dedicated fields populated where necessary, compatible metadata during the stated window, and new agents using the immutable fields.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: The dedicated fields are immutable immediately after creation; metadata updates remain accepted by validation but ignored by new agents; N is the upgrade's introduction release.

R_claim_support.claim: Existing profile-selection meaning and dedicated field context
Creation cases and N+4 backfill removal

caveats: Workload in R means the Pod object in the frozen target; it does not extend these rules to policies or templates.
N+4 belongs to the workload creation backfill; the separate policy N+1 window is not substituted or merged.
This is a representation transition for existing profile functionality, with the source's explicit annotation-update behavior change retained.
No default-profile change, new confinement semantics, new profile source, or corrected API type spelling is introduced.
Fields become immutable after object creation, not only after the N+4 transition.

R_fidelity_review.input: An already implemented feature gate and the existing node-condition eviction and duration settings.
R_fidelity_review.state: The feature already implements eviction and toleration behavior; the proposal requests a default-enabled graduation transition.
R_fidelity_review.action: Enable the feature by default, confirm adequate coverage, and update maturity-status documentation.
R_fidelity_review.output: The same existing eviction behavior is enabled by default, with coverage and documentation prepared for graduation.
R_fidelity_review.invariants: No eviction algorithm or duration semantics change is introduced.

R_claim_support.claim: Default-on gate change, coverage, and documentation

caveats: The pre-existing eviction mechanism is explicitly treated as baseline rather than as a newly proposed design.
No exact gate identifier, implementation diff, rollout sequence, new coverage threshold, or functional test matrix is invented.
The query does not imply that the initial snapshot introduced the underlying feature.
